sections.text:
The great story begins before the creation of humanity, when the universe was teeming with honorable angels who worshiped God and never disobeyed Him.

God Almighty informed His angels of a great decision, and He said to them: “Indeed, I will place a caliph on earth.”

The angels were astonished by this decision, and they asked God an inquiring question without objection: “Will You place therein someone who will cause corruption and shed blood?”

God, with His vast knowledge surrounding everything, answered them: “Indeed, I know what you do not know.”

Thus, God Almighty ordered the collection of dust from all parts of the earth, and the dirt came in different colors, including red, white, black, plain, and sad.

This is the reason why people have different colors and natures to this day.

He mixed the dirt with water and it became clay, and God Almighty shaped it with His generous hand into the best shape.

He left the clay until it dried and became like pottery, then God breathed His spirit into it, and life came into Adam’s body, peace be upon him.

The first thing Adam did after the spirit entered him and he sneezed was to say: “Praise be to God,” and his Lord replied to him: “Your Lord have mercy on you, Adam.”

God wanted to show Adam's virtue and status to the angels, so he taught him the names of all things.

He taught Adam the names of mountains, trees, animals, and everything in existence, a knowledge that the angels did not know.

God presented these things to the angels and asked them about their names, but they were unable and said: “Glory be to You. We have no knowledge except what You have taught us.”

Then God commanded Adam to tell them their names, and when he did, the angels realized the virtue of this new creature and the greatness of God’s wisdom in his creation.

In honor of Adam, God commanded all the angels to prostrate to him, a prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of worship.

The angels obeyed the command of their Lord and all prostrated, except for Iblis, who lived with them even though he was a jinn.

Satan was arrogant and refused to prostrate, and he said arrogantly: “I am better than him. You created me from fire and you created him from clay.”

God was angry with Satan and expelled him from His mercy and cursed him until the Day of Judgment.

The cursed Satan asked God to give him time until the Day of Resurrection to tempt Adam and his descendants, so God gave him time.

God made Adam live in Paradise, but he felt lonely, so God created his wife Eve from his rib to live with him.

Adam and Eve lived in Paradise enjoying its fruits and drinking from its rivers with great happiness.

God permitted them to do everything in Paradise except for one tree. He warned them not to approach it or eat from its fruits.

Here the cursed Satan began implementing his malicious plan to trap Adam and Eve.

He began whispering to them and swearing that he was their advisor, and he was led to believe that eating from the tree would make them immortal.

Adam and Eve were weak in the face of Satan’s temptation and his false oath, so they forgot their Lord’s warning and picked the fruits of the forbidden tree.

As soon as they ate from it, their private parts were exposed and they felt extremely ashamed, and they began to cover their bodies with the leaves of the trees of paradise.

God called out to them, admonishing them: “Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is your clear enemy?”

Adam and Eve realized the great mistake they had made, and they deeply regretted it, and prayed to God with words of repentance.

They said: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will certainly be among the losers.”

God accepted their repentance with His vast mercy, but He decreed that they should descend to Earth to begin the journey of humanity and the architecture of the universe.

Adam and Eve descended to earth and began their new life that required hard work for food and shelter.

God blessed them with offspring, and Adam began teaching his children agriculture, industry, and how to live.

Adam, peace be upon him, taught his children to unite God, worship Him, and stay away from the steps of Satan.

Years passed, and Adam and Eve experienced a harsh ordeal when their son Cain killed his brother Abel out of envy.

Adam was deeply saddened by the loss of his righteous son, but he continued to direct his descendants to righteousness and piety.

Adam lived a long life, and he saw his great-grandchildren, and he taught them that this world is a place of testing and that Paradise is a place of decision.

When his time came, the angels of death came to take his soul, and his children cried, but the angels washed him, shrouded him, and taught his children how to bury the dead.

Thus ended the story of the father of humans, leaving behind him descendants who will inhabit the earth and engage in an eternal struggle between good and evil.

The moral of the story is a warning against the arrogance and arrogance that destroyed Satan, and the importance of quick repentance when one makes a mistake, as Adam did.

We also learn that Satan is the first enemy of man, and that obedience to God is the only way to salvation.
